title: Weak point Wednesday: Calves
summary: He argues calves are not purely genetic: insertions change the look, not whether they can grow, and calves resist growth because daily walking already loads them heavily. His current approach is a three-part attack: a heavy low-rep day, a light nucleus overload day supersetted into upper-body sessions, and seated raises with a weighted stretch.
claims: His biggest bodybuilding regret is not training his calves sooner
Calves are not 100% genetic despite the common belief
Low calf insertions give more muscle to develop and more size potential, while short insertions let the mass pop and look more 3D
Bad insertions limit absolute size and strength but do not decide whether your calves can make your legs look beefy instead of like chicken legs
Genetic potential is only revealed by work; a dominant muscle usually reflects how much it was trained, not great genetics
The body parts that grew most on him, biceps and abs, are the ones he trained like a madman
Many people with big calves used to be fat, so they carried extra weight on their legs every day
Calves are resistant because everyone uses them constantly; untrained calves already measure 13-14 inches of mostly lean mass, while untrained arms rarely reach 15
Calves get more tonnage from everyday activity than any other muscle, so a few calf raises add too little absolute tonnage to trigger growth
His calves are 16 inches without ever training them, grown through sports; he is aiming for 18 inches to match his upper legs
He used to do a heavy and a medium calf day at the end of workouts but skipped them; now a light nucleus overload calf superset sits between sets on upper-body day so he cannot escape it
Have a heavy calf day using heavy exercises and lower rep ranges, on a calf machine or a barbell setup at home
A calf raise is an exaggerated step; bodyweight calf raises add too little over the millions of steps you already take
Make bodyweight calf raises harder with single-leg reps, slow negatives, burnout sets, working off a ledge with a stretch at the bottom and a squeeze at the top
For nucleus overload he holds just a 10 lb plate for very high reps, accumulating tonnage without turning it into strength work
Seated calf raises with an EZ bar on the knees (25 lb per side), feet elevated, to failure, then pressing down on the bar to load the stretch on the exhausted calves
exercises: off a ledge, stretch at bottom, squeeze at top, slow negatives
harder than bodyweight raises on two legs
Calf raise holding a 10 lb plate
nucleus overload without becoming strength work
Seated EZ-bar calf raise with weighted stretch
feet elevated; at failure press on the bar to stretch
Heavy barbell or machine calf raise
